findings.where: the whole sheet, y33-3043 x79-1363, and the ground behind it
findings.what: The setup sheet is one exact colour: RGB(242,237,226) covers 2,321,628 of 4,492,800 pixels (51.7% of the screen) and a 220x260 patch at y900-1120 x300-560 measures std 0.0000 over a single unique value, with a second exact colour RGB(76,62,50) filling another 22.6% behind it, so 74.3% of this screen is two flat fills with a drawn deckle edge stuck on the join.
findings.why: This is the named failure of anti-goal four: a surface that reads as an approximation of paper rather than as a photograph of real paper, and it is the first screen an iPhone owner meets.

findings.where: the row of received feelings, y1150-1560; 'hold' at x760-960 and 'goodnight' at x1190-1440
findings.what: The feeling objects are untextured CG props sitting on textured paper: a 24x24 patch inside the 'hold' candle (y1250-1274 x820-844) measures std 0.44 and one inside the 'goodnight' card (y1300-1324 x1260-1284) measures std 0.72, against std 7.68 for the same size patch on the 'ugh' paper note beside them (y1230-1254 x340-364); the candle shows visible polygon facets on its silhouette and the 'goodnight' object is a flat pale-grey rectangle with a hard offset drop shadow and a folded white corner.
findings.why: A flat rectangle with a drop shadow standing in for a card is the exact substitute anti-goal four forbids, and an untextured render standing in for the sensation is the emotional layer leaning on generic art rather than on a real object.

findings.where: 'nyeh' at x980-1220 y1220-1400 and 'confetti' at x500-780 y1180-1400 (same objects again in crops/dusk_pulse.png)
findings.what: 'nyeh' renders as a glossy pink tongue-shaped blob with a broad specular highlight and no fold, edge or grain, and 'confetti' renders as twelve smooth pastel ellipsoids with cast shadows and no paper edge; neither reads as the paper object it is named after (logs/haptics.json binds them to obj_wrapper and obj_confetti).
findings.why: A glossy pink tongue and a scatter of smooth pastel balls are emoji shapes rendered in 3D, which is anti-goal two operating inside the emotional layer itself.

findings.where: the masonry grid, e.g. the frame at x490-930 y1330-1720, and the opened image in 14_media_viewer.png
findings.what: The images standing in for the couple's photographs are abstract CG renders - a flat grey sky band over a black plane with a glowing sphere, untextured bowls on a wood plane - not photographs; evidence/logs/manifest.json separately lists five seed/photos/*.jpg entries with no file on disk while still reporting "ok": true.
findings.why: Generic 3D renders filling the memory layer are stock imagery standing in for the couple's own material, and the evidence gives no screen where a real photograph appears.

findings.what: The voice check is {"strings_read": 116, "findings": [], "ok": true} - it names no rule it applied and lists none of the 116 strings, so nothing in it can be checked against the pictures; the roughly ninety strings legible in the ten screenshots had to be read by eye instead.
findings.why: Anti-goal three is about every string the app displays, and an unenumerated pass claim leaves most of them unverifiable from evidence alone.

findings.where: the objects family, entry objects/obj_gold_star.webp, patch_std 28.59
findings.what: A gold star surface ships in the object inventory; it is bound to none of the 36 feelings in logs/haptics.json and appears in none of the fifteen artifacts, so it is present in the build but never shown.
findings.why: A gold star is the canonical reward token, and anti-goal one is about engagement machinery appearing anywhere in the build, not only on screen.

findings.what: The shelf glance reads "waiting on you: the one you said you stopped" - the one string in the evidence that points at something the reader failed to keep doing; it sits below the fold and is not visible in 03_us.png.
findings.why: Anti-goal one forbids guilt, and a glance that names a thing you stopped is the nearest the build comes to a nudge, even if it is phrased as a fact.

findings.where: the desk, x200-1000 y1900-2500 at native resolution
findings.what: The ground under every sheet is smooth two-tone grain bands with a drawn elliptical knot and three straight white scratch strokes and no pores or dust; autocorrelation over y1750-2600 x100-1340 finds no tiling (strongest horizontal lag peak 0.136, vertical decay monotonic), so it is not a repeating tile, but it is an illustration of wood rather than a photograph of it.
findings.why: Anti-goal four names paper specifically, so this is not a direct breach, but the desk is the ground of every screen and its drawn quality pulls the real paper on top of it toward the same reading.

what_is_working: No exclamation mark occurs anywhere in evidence/logs/*.json and the word 'user' occurs nowhere; the ten screenshots contain no marketing sentence and no 'Oops!'.

Failure and emptiness are written in the app's own register: 'it would not go x' in 13_messenger_states.png, 'nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone.' in 10_first_run.png, 'nothing from them since you last looked' in logs/10_first_run.report.json.

The tab bar in all ten screenshots carries no badge, dot or counter, and the rituals module's glance is 'last: tuesday soup' (logs/03_us.report.json) rather than a streak length - the one place a streak counter would normally sit.

No emoji appears in any artifact: reactions render as plain grey Blu-Tack discs (13_messenger_states.png, y1780-1960 x220-700) and delivery state is written out as 'sent' with one ink tick and 'read' with two, drawn in the same hand as the text.
The 36 feeling names in logs/haptics.json are lowercase plain speech - 'miss you', "it's okay", "i'll make you tea", 'long day', 'not okay' - with no emoji, no title case and no invented brand words.

The chat and pulse paper is genuinely textured: logs/surfaces.json lists 54 paper surfaces at patch_std 2.29-11.56 over a 1.2 floor, and a 24x24 patch on the 'ugh' note in 01_pulse.png measures std 7.68 while crops/02_chat_300_edge.png shows fibre standing off the tear.
The app never names itself in any string on screen; logs/pwa.json shows the manifest name is 'the other phone', a description rather than a brand.

The setup copy in 17_setup_pwa.png is instruction rather than persuasion - 'say them out loud in the same room. they are only good once.', 'it will not hold on to anything until you do.' - with no benefit claims and no addressing of the reader as a customer.
verdict: Three of the four anti-goals are held, and two of them are held well. There is no engagement machinery in anything the evidence shows: no badges, no counters on the tab bar, no points, and the rituals module reports 'last: tuesday soup' where a streak count would sit; the only blemishes are a shipped but unused obj_gold_star.webp in the surface inventory and one below-the-fold shelf glance that names something the reader stopped. The voice is the strongest part of the build - no exclamation mark anywhere in the logs, the word 'user' nowhere, errors written as 'it would not go', the app never naming itself - though evidence/logs/strings.json asserts that pass over 116 strings without listing one of them, so only the strings legible in the artifacts are actually checkable. There is no emoji soup: reactions are grey Blu-Tack discs and delivery state is ink ticks. What costs the build here is the fourth anti-goal and the material of the emotional layer. 17_setup_pwa.png is not paper at all: one exact colour covers 51.7% of the screen, a 220x260 patch of the sheet measures std 0.0000 over a single unique value, and a second exact colour fills 22.6% behind it, so the screen that welcomes the Apple half of the product is a flat cream fill with a drawn deckle edge on a flat brown ground. Alongside it, the objects that carry the feelings are untextured CG props - the candle interior at std 0.44 and the 'goodnight' dog-ear at std 0.72 against 7.68 for the paper beside them, the latter a flat rectangle with a hard drop shadow - and 'nyeh' and 'confetti' read as 3D emoji rather than as things off a desk. Because simulated paper is scored twice by design, and because it here coincides with the emotional layer leaning on generic renders, this category cannot meet its floor of 9.
